The code of a table's plan, from its definition

Source: R/spec_code.R
tfl_table_code.Rd

Writes the rtfreporter::table_plan() pipeline a table definition stands for, one pipe from the ARD: rtfreporter::normalize_ard() (the hierarchy, the overall row and the stack the definitions say), the roles of its tables sheet in table_plan(), and one plan_*() verb for each thing the other sheets say – the same verbs, with the same values, that tfl_table_plan(data, spec) applies. The program then no longer reads the workbook, and what the workbook cannot say (a cell style, a step after the pages are made) is written under it by hand. tfl_as_table_spec() goes the other way.

Usage

tfl_table_code(
  spec,
  output_id = NULL,
  data = "ard",
  plan = "plan",
  pipe = NULL,
  ard_spec = NULL,
  normalize = TRUE
)

Arguments

spec

A table definition (tfl_read_table_spec(), tfl_table_spec()), or the path(s) of its workbook(s).

output_id

The table, when the definition has several.

data

The name of the ARD in the program: the pipe starts from it (plan <- ard |> normalize_ard(...) |> table_plan(...)). With normalize = FALSE, the name of the data already normalized.

plan

The name the plan is assigned to.

pipe

"|>", "%>%" or "rstudio" (RStudio's Insert Pipe Operator); NULL follows getOption("rtfreporter.ard_pipe"), else "|>" (see rtfreporter::plan_template()).

ard_spec

The ARD definition (tfl_read_ard_spec()), for rtfreporter::normalize_ard()'s hierarchy; NULL for none.

normalize

TRUE to write rtfreporter::normalize_ard() at the head of the pipe (its hierarchy, overall and stack from the definitions); FALSE when the program normalizes the ARD itself (tfl_normalize_code()).

Value

The code, one element per line.

See also

tfl_report_code() for the report around it.

Examples

spec <- tfl_read_table_spec(
  system.file("extdata", "ard-spec", "DM.xlsx", package = "tflspec"))
cat(tfl_table_code(spec), sep = "\n")
#> # the code lists: each value in its order, as the table shows it
#> cl_agegr1 <- c("<65", ">=65")
#> cl_sex <- c("F", "M")
#> cl_ecogbl <- c("0", "1")
#> 
#> plan <- ard |>
#>   normalize_ard() |>
#>   table_plan(cols = "TRT01A", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
#>   plan_cells(
#>     continuous = list(
#>       n = "{N:.0f}",
#>       "Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
#>       Median = "{median:.1f}",
#>       "Min, Max" = "{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"
#>     ),
#>     categorical = "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})"
#>   ) |>
#>   plan_levels(
#>     variable = c("AGE", "AGEGR1", "SEX", "RACE", "ECOGBL", "BSLD"),
#>     AGEGR1 = cl_agegr1,
#>     SEX = cl_sex,
#>     ECOGBL = cl_ecogbl
#>   ) |>
#>   plan_labels(
#>     variable = c(
#>       AGE = "Age (years)",
#>       AGEGR1 = "Age group, n (%)",
#>       SEX = "Sex, n (%)",
#>       RACE = "Race, n (%)",
#>       ECOGBL = "Baseline ECOG performance status, n (%)",
#>       BSLD = "Baseline sum of diameters (mm)"
#>     )
#>   ) |>
#>   plan_digits(rounding = "sas") |>
#>   plan_col_header(
#>     data.frame(
#>       line = c("1", "1", "2", "2"),
#>       cols = c("row_label", ".values", "row_label", ".values"),
#>       span = c(NA, "each", NA, "each"),
#>       text = c(NA, "{col}", "Parameter", "(N={n})")
#>     )
#>   ) |>
#>   plan_stub(name = "row_label", before = TRUE) |>
#>   plan_blanks(where = "between_groups", first = TRUE, last = FALSE) |>
#>   plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 30, split = "group_safe") |>
#>   plan_columns(widths = c(row_label = 4, .values = 2)) |>
#>   plan_style(align_count_pct = TRUE)
